question: How many orbital launches will SpaceX conduct between October 1 and October 3, 2026 (inclusive)?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: 3-day windows in Aug-Sep 2026 at a reduced Falcon cadence (~0.25-0.3 launches/day as Starlink moves to Vandenberg and LC-39A shifts to Starship), giving ~0.8-0.9 per 3 days. The window has specific scheduled launches: Crew-13 is set for Oct 1 15:10 UTC from CCSFS (already delayed from Sept 12 by an oxidizer leak that has been fixed; 3 days of backup chances; ~0.7 to fly in window). Transporter-18 is listed NET Oct 1 TBC by rocketlaunch.org but Oct 31 elsewhere (~0.3). An unlisted Vandenberg Starlink could fill the Sept 26 to Oct 10 gap. No Starship in the window. No human market found; the Manifold candidates (2027 launch share; Crew-13 by Sept 30) do not match this question. Estimated PMF: 0:0.15, 1:0.42, 2:0.33, 3:0.09, 4+:0.01.
calls.dossier:
- Crew-13 (Falcon 9/Crew Dragon, CCSFS SLC-40): targeted Oct 1 2026 15:10 UTC (Spaceflight Now schedule; rocketlaunch.org; NextSpaceflight; 3DNews 2026-09-23). Delayed from Sept 12 by an oxidizer leak in the Dragon propulsion system, since repaired and verified. Docking planned Oct 2.
- Transporter-18 (Falcon 9 SSO rideshare, Vandenberg): rocketlaunch.org mission page lists NET Oct 1 18:08 UTC, 'TBC'. spacelaunchschedule.com/search snippet lists Oct 31 2026. Spaceflight Now and NextSpaceflight do not list it in the window. Conflicting.
- USSF-385 (F9, Vandenberg SLC-4E, B1096 10th flight): Sept 26 11:56 UTC (Spaceflight Now; rocketlaunch.org).
- Starship Flight 14: Sept 28 ~12:15-13:15 UTC, Starbase, before the window. A slip of 3+ days would bring it into the window (Space.com 2026-09-23; FAA approval pending).
- Starlink 15-25 (Vandenberg): Oct 10 (Spaceflight Now; rocketlaunch.org). No Starlink launches are listed between Sept 26 and Oct 10 as of Sept 23. Starlink launches are often added to public schedules only about 1-2 weeks ahead.
- Cadence: 2026 Falcon pace ~140-145/yr vs 165 in 2025. 80 of 103 F9 flights in 2026 were Starlink. The slowdown is deliberate: LC-39A is steered toward Starship/FH, droneships are being reshuffled, and Starlink is concentrated at Vandenberg (TeslaNorth 2026-08-23 and search summaries). September 2026 launch dates: Sept 2, 6, 10, 13, 16, ~20, then 26 (about one every 3-4 days, ~0.25-0.3/day).
- Base rate over all 3-day windows at the 2026 annual pace (~0.39/day): ~1.2 launches per window. Over the recent Aug-Sep regime: ~0.8-0.9 per window. Conditional component: Crew-13 is scheduled on day 1 of the window with 2 more days of backup.
- Crewed Dragon launches historically slip often by 1+ days (weather at the launch site and along the abort corridor, technical issues). A slip beyond 3 days would take it out of the window.
- Resolution: resolves off the Wikipedia 'List of Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launches' 2026 section by UTC liftoff date, plus any Starship orbital launch. Scrubs do not count.
- Event window: Oct 1 00:00 UTC -> Oct 3 23:59 UTC per the criteria; as of Sept 23 23:50 UTC, 0% elapsed (window starts in ~7 days).
- Searched but could not find: an authoritative Transporter-18 date, Florida Starlink launches in late Sept/early Oct, and any human prediction market on this count.

calls.reasoning: SpaceX's recent pace sets the prior. Since Falcon 9 Starlink launches from Florida ended in August 2026, Falcon has launched about once every 3-4 days, or about 0.8 launches per random 3-day window. This window is not random, though. Crew-13 is firmly targeted for Oct 1 at 15:10 UTC, its oxidizer leak is fixed, and Oct 2-3 give it backup days. I put about 0.68 on it lifting off in the window, allowing for weather slips and the history of crewed-launch slips. Transporter-18 is listed for Oct 1 by some sources and Oct 31 by others, and rideshare missions slip often, so I give it about 0.30. A Starlink or other mission not yet on public schedules could fill the Sep 26–Oct 10 gap at Vandenberg (about 0.25). Starship Flight 14 slipping from Sep 28 into exactly Oct 1-3 is about 0.12. The expected count is about 1.35. The most likely outcome is 1, and P(0) is about 15%. No human market prices this window.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on the facts about Crew-13: Oct 1 at 15:10 UTC, leak repaired. They split on four questions. First, the Transporter-18 date (Oct 1 TBC vs Oct 31). The runs even disagree about which site said which date, and I can't settle this without web access, so it stays at about 0.30. That is below Run 3's 0.5 because two of the three schedules checked did not list it in the window. Second, whether an unlisted launch fills the gap. This is a judgment call. SLC-4E is booked Sep 26 and Oct 10 and the regime is slower, but Starlink missions often go public late, so about 0.25. Third, Starship slipping into the window: Runs 2 and 3 agree on about 0.12, and I keep that. Fourth, Run 1 assumed no Starship in the window. I treat that as a judgment it didn't argue for, and I overrule it because FAA approval is still pending. The combined estimate sits close to Runs 1 and 2 and below Run 3, because I give Transporter-18 and unlisted launches lower odds than Run 3 did. No market was retrieved on this run. The Manifold candidates the harness surfaced (a 2027 launch-share market and Crew-13 by Sep 30) do not match this question's contract.
